newsitem.title: CROATIA: Red Cross in Croatia mourns dead in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross in Croatia mourns dead in Chechnya.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross shut down operations in Croatia for one day on Friday to mourn the murder of six colleagues in Chechnya.

An ICRC statement said flags at its six offices in Croatia flew at half mast. The ICRC has a significant presence in Croatia and nearby Bosnia because of wars that followed the breakup of old Yugoslavia, ending in 1995.
The six aid workers, five of them women, were shot in their beds in a Red Cross hospital compound in the village of Novye Atagi near the Chechnya capital Grozny on Tuesday.
It was the worst attack on the Geneva-based ICRC in its 142-year history.
The security service of Chechnya's separatist government said on Friday it had detained several people suspected of involvement in the murders, Itar-Tass news agency said.
